nodes.summary: The union of the edges of the cube $[-1, 1]^3$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$: the set of points $x$ with every coordinate in $[-1, 1]$ such that at least two distinct coordinates $x_i$ and $x_j$ are each equal to $1$ or $-1$.
nodes.title: Edges of the cube $(-1, 1)^3$

nodes.summary: The closed cube $[-1, 1]^3$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$: the set of points of three-dimensional Euclidean space all of whose coordinates lie in $[-1, 1]$.
nodes.title: The closed cube $(-1, 1)^3$

nodes.summary: There exist an open set $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ whose interior contains the closed cube $[-1, 1]^3$ and a function $f : \mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}$ that is harmonic at every point of $U$, vanishes at every point of the edges of the cube $[-1, 1]^3$, and satisfies $f(x) \neq 0$ for some $x \in U$.
nodes.title: Scottish Book Problem 151: a harmonic function vanishing on the edges of a cube
